name: English (US)
title: Vulcan Celox | Claude Code, Codex, and local projects
description: A local workspace for developers working with Claude Code and Codex. Bring terminals, sessions, code, PHP projects, and Node apps together on your Mac.
headline: Which agent is waiting, and which branch still needs a push?
intro: Vulcan Celox brings Claude Code and Codex sessions, terminals, prompts, and local projects together in a native Mac app.
imageNote: Actual product interface, using demonstration data.
stackLabel: Works with the tools you already use
productBody: When each agent lives in a different window and each project in another folder, context gets scattered. Celox brings your local work together and makes the connections visible.

workflow.title: Open your project
workflow.text: Find PHP sites, add Node projects, or open a folder. Each terminal starts in the right place.

workflow.title: Work with your agents
workflow.text: Choose Claude Code or Codex for that tab. Follow sessions, requests, files, and commands without switching tools.

workflow.title: Come back with context
workflow.text: Resume a session, read the terminal's memory, and see what changed before continuing.

terminalBody: Open a shell or choose the agent for that session. Split the panel, search the output, and return to your project without losing your open terminals.

Prompts are pasted without an automatic Enter

localBody: The app reads local agent logs to organize context. It doesn't require an API key to follow Claude Code and Codex, and it doesn't write to their configuration folders.

privacy.title: Your data stays with you

privacy.title: Connections with a purpose
privacy.text: PR and update checks have their own controls. AI documentation runs only when you request it, using your Anthropic key.

privacy.title: Transparency in the source
privacy.text: Read the project, licenses, and documentation. Celox is open source under the MIT license.

environmentTitle: PHP and Node in one workspace.
environmentBody: Use Lerd or Laravel Valet for local PHP development. Add Node projects, see their scripts, and open commands in the terminal. No PHP installed? Terminals, agents, and organization are still available.
environmentItems: PHP sites, versions, and local HTTPS through your backend
languagesBody: Choose Português (Brasil), English (US), or Español (España) in Settings. You don't need to install three separate apps.
installBody: Download the app, open a folder, and start with the tools you already know.
requirements: macOS 13 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel, and Python 3.9+. The app guides you through installing Python if needed. Claude Code, Codex, and environment backends are installed separately.
downloadNote: The button opens the distribution available on GitHub. Check its version and requirements before installing.

installSteps.title: Open Celox
installSteps.text: Choose your language and find your projects. Local data stays separate from the application.

installSteps.title: Open your first terminal

faq.q: Does Celox replace Claude Code or Codex?
faq.a: No. It organizes projects, terminals, and sessions around the tools you already use. Your agents still run through their own programs and accounts.

faq.q: Do I need an API key?
faq.a: Not to read and follow local Claude Code and Codex sessions. The optional AI documentation feature uses your Anthropic key and runs only when you request it.

faq.q: Can I edit files inside the app?
faq.a: The Code screen is a read-only viewer with a tree, search, live following, and diffs. Use your external editor for changes. Celox doesn't promise file saving in that screen.

faq.q: Do I need to install Lerd?
faq.a: Only if you want to use it as the backend for local PHP sites. Laravel Valet is also supported. Node projects, terminals, agents, and organization work without either backend.
The stable experience is built for macOS. Linux and Windows distributions are prereleases; check the requirements and limitations published in the repository.

App data is local. Optional features contact external services, such as GitHub for PRs and versions and Anthropic for documentation you request. The agents themselves follow their own services and settings.

The link to a tab uses folder and timing. Sessions started almost together in the same folder can be matched to the wrong tab. This limitation is documented and doesn't change the per-tab decision to start an agent.
Yes. Celox source code is distributed under the MIT license. Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices in the repository.
